newsitem.title: GERMANY: Arbitrators propose German rail pay compromise.
newsitem.headline: Arbitrators propose German rail pay compromise.

text.p: Arbitrators seeking to resolve a dispute over pay for 180,000 German railway workers have announced a compromise proposal which both unions and employers signalled could be acceptable.

Arbitration committee chief Harro Plander told journalists the committee on Saturday night proposed a rise of 1.3 percent in west German railway workers' wages from May 1997 and an earlier one-off bonus payment of 300 marks ($202) per worker.
The proposed contract would run until April 1998.
East German railway workers would have their pay increased to 86 percent of west German levels from the start of 1998, compared with 84 percent now.

The 95,000 east German workers would also receive a one-off bonus payment of 250 marks and see their supplementary payments increased to 100 percent of west German levels from January 1997, Plander said.
The arbitrators' proposal will be discussed at talks between union and employer representatives on Thursday.

The proposed deal for west German workers was little changed in its basic terms from an offer the union had earlier rejected. But rail union officials said improvements in the offer for east Germany made the package more palatable.
Rudi Schaefer, chairman of Germany's main railway workers' union, the GdED, said the union was particularly pleased with the outcome of the proposal for east Germany.
Horst Foehr, personnel executive at Deutsche Bahn, said the east German element of the deal was the hardest part for the company to accept.
He said he nonetheless intended to recommend that the company's management board accept the pay deal. ($1=1.4854 Mark)
